newsitem.title: GERMANY: Opel works council against pension changes.
newsitem.headline: Opel works council against pension changes.

text.p: The works council of Adam Opel AG, the German unit of General Motors Corp, said on Friday that it opposed proposals to reduce retirement benefits for new employees.

The works council said the proposal was put foward by Opel management at a meeting on Friday and that it did not believe, as claimed by Opel management, that the plan would lead to significant cost savings.
Opel said it was seeking to trim benefits to justifiable levels based on industry conditions and in a bid to keep the carmaker competitive at a time of weakening profits.
It said the proposal, which it would seek to include in future wage contracts, would apply only to new employees and not to existing pensioners or current employees.
Opel said retirement benefits account for about 12 percent of its wage costs, which it said was well above the average in German industry.
On Thursday Opel said sales in 1996 rose 9.3 percent to 28.3 billion marks but it expected weaker profits for the year due to stiff competition and saw few prospects for any improvement in 1997.
